entrypoints.summary: The menu protocol accepts movie creation/sharing/display, friend creation/removal, and account-deletion feedback operations.
The supplied container serves the binary through socat on TCP port 1337.

negative_controls: No vulnerable-versus-fixed regression run is provided.
The packaged flag fixture identifies a local challenge oracle but is not evidence that a specific execution was run during extraction.
observability.positive_marker: The writeup shows an interactive shell and a successful cat flag.txt result.

preconditions: The target is the supplied allocator-sensitive challenge runtime; the container artifact uses Ubuntu 20.10 and serves Plaidflix on TCP port 1337.
The attacker can operate the menu protocol and perform ordered movie/friend/feedback actions.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Two short friend names, one movie shared with the second friend, followed by friend removals and movie display.
trigger_steps.summary: Create friends, share a movie with one, remove the friends, and display the movie to consume the stale shared-friend reference.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Repeated feedback creation/deletion plus structured chunk-header and pointer payloads.
trigger_steps.summary: Use retained feedback entries and controlled feedback/contact payloads to groom allocator state and corrupt tcache links toward __free_hook.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A NUL-terminated /bin/sh string followed by system pointer payloads.
trigger_steps.summary: Allocate a /bin/sh feedback payload, write system through the redirected allocation, then delete the command-bearing feedback.

mitigations.concept: invalidate all aliases before freeing objects

The documented spawned shell runs cat flag.txt and displays the challenge flag.

relation_candidates.dst: invalidate all aliases before freeing objects
relation_candidates.rationale: Removing or invalidating movie references before friend deallocation prevents movie display from reaching the freed friend.

impact.affected_asset: Integrity of the Plaidflix process control flow and confidentiality of flag.txt readable by the service account.
impact.attacker_capability: A remote menu client can obtain heap/libc address disclosures, redirect allocation through __free_hook, install system as the free hook, and trigger system("/bin/sh").
impact.security_effect: Documented arbitrary code execution in the challenge service process, followed by reading its packaged flag fixture.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker can share a movie with a friend and later remove that friend through menu operations.
Removing a friend frees it without removing it from a movie that was shared with it; separately, deleted feedback pointers remain retained and can be freed repeatedly.

Displaying a movie dereferences the retained freed-friend object and exposes allocator pointer content; repeated feedback frees and heap grooming create chunk misalignment that permits modification of a tcache entry's forward and back pointers.
The documented exploit directs tcache allocation to __free_hook, writes system there, and frees a feedback buffer containing /bin/sh, yielding an interactive shell that reads the challenge flag.

failure.operation: Stale-object display discloses freed allocator contents; repeated freeing of retained feedback pointers enables overlap-driven tcache-link corruption.

primary_invariant.statement: A freed friend must not remain reachable through a movie, and a freed feedback allocation must not remain reusable through the feedback collection.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Friend removal leaves the movie's shared-friend reference intact, while feedback deletion leaves its pointer present for subsequent frees.

quality.review_notes: The mechanism is supported by a public writeup and exploit script, including a documented successful shell session, but organizer source, a remediation patch, and regression tests are absent. The claimed endpoint is allocator/libc-version-specific; this CTF result should not be generalized to a deployed product. No enumerated harness category precisely represents the supplied interactive end-to-end exploit, so harness_fit remains none_known.

remediation.invariant_restored: Before freeing a friend, remove or invalidate all movie references to it; when deleting feedback, remove or null its collection entry so no later menu action can free the allocation again.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Ubuntu 20.10 container exposing the supplied Plaidflix binary

target.component: movie/friend sharing and account-deletion feedback management
